commits_this_run: 06b5b32 fix(agents): report the exact trail size on the tool-invocation audit page (NEX-088)
decisions_this_run: A second port method, not a len() over a bigger page: 'how many rows match' has an exact aggregate answer, and deriving it from a page makes correctness a function of volume (same reasoning as NEX-082/NEX-087).
Return a page object (ToolInvocationAuditPage) from the use case rather than a tuple, matching NotePage, so the total cannot be dropped at the call site by accident.

Justify each surviving PageMeta(total=len(items)) site individually rather than converting all of them: all five are unpaginated, so page size IS the total and the number is honest. Converting them would add endpoints nobody asked for.
The count is in the same transaction as the page, but that is atomicity, not a single snapshot - under READ COMMITTED an insert can land between the two statements. The docstring says so.
run_summary: Run 88 swept the derived-value audit surfaces and fixed 'GET /agents/{agent_id}/tool-invocations reported meta.total with len(items), so each page claimed its own window was the whole trail. A three-entry trail answered 2 then 1. The port gained count_for_agent (SELECT count(*) scoped to the agent), ListToolInvocations returns a page carrying the true total, and the router fills PageMeta.total from it. Mutation found that an unscoped count survived the first regression test - a worse bug that would disclose another agent's trail size - so a second test pins the scope; both mutations now fail. The four sibling total=len(items) listings were each verified unpaginated and left alone. ruff/mypy clean, full pytest exit 0 twice. Product 06b5b32 pushed and remote-verified.
